name: Import a backup file
description: Merges an export file (see export.json) into the data. Nothing that already exists is changed or deleted, so importing into empty data is a full restore. Each item is saved on its own: importing the same file again creates nothing, and a retry after a failure part-way through is safe.

request.body: An export file, exactly as GET /api/export returns it. At most 50 MB, 5,000 categories and 20,000 links.

responses.description: Something was created. (200 with the same body when nothing was.) index is the 1-based position in the file's categories or links array; meta counts the entries in the file.
Not an export file. Nothing is written.

details.message: This isn't a Link Organizer export file.

rules: format must be "link-organizer-export" (field format: "This isn't a Link Organizer export file."), version must be 1 (field version), categories and links must be arrays of at most 5,000 and 20,000 entries (field categories / links). Breaking any of these rejects the whole request with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED.

Categories, parents first: an id that already exists is used as is (existing). Otherwise a category with the same name (case-insensitive) under the same parent is reused (merged). Otherwise it's created with the file's id, name and timestamps.

A parentId in neither the file nor the data, or one that forms a cycle, makes the category top-level. A category entry with an invalid id or name is skipped (VALIDATION_FAILED); its subcategories become top-level and its links unsorted.

Links, in file order: a URL that's already saved, or repeated earlier in the file, is skipped with DUPLICATE_URL. The create rules apply (notes sanitized); a link that breaks one is skipped with VALIDATION_FAILED.

A link keeps its id unless it's taken (then it gets a new one), and keeps createdAt/updatedAt when they're valid ISO timestamps. Its categoryId follows the category mapping; an unknown category makes it unsorted.
rating in the file is 1-5 or null (not rated).
